いつも通りの時間に目を覚ます。
六時前。
夜明けを迎えたばかりの空は薄暗く、今日も灰色の雲で覆われていた。

pages.en:
I wake at the usual hour.

It is not yet six.

Dawn has only just broken. The sky remains dim, covered once more by gray clouds.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I wake up up at the same time as usual.
It’s before six o’clock.
The day is dawning, and the sky is filled with gray clouds again.

pages.ja: 左腕に痛みはない。
pages.jaRuby: 左腕に痛みはない。
pages.en: There is no pain in my left arm.
pages.mirrorMoon: I don’t feel any pain from my left arm.

pages.ja:
居間には誰もいない。
遠坂が起きてくる前に朝食を作っておかなくては。
pages.jaRuby:
居間には誰もいない。
遠坂が起きてくる前に朝食を作っておかなくては。
pages.en:
The living room is empty.

I need to make breakfast before Tohsaka wakes.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There’s no one in the living room.
I should make breakfast before Tohsaka wakes up.

pages.ja:
ニュースが流れている。
朝方、こうしてテレビをチェックするのが日課になりつつある。
pages.jaRuby:
ニュースが流れている。
朝方、こうしてテレビをチェックするのが日課になりつつある。
pages.en:
The news is playing.

Checking the television this early is becoming part of my daily routine.
pages.mirrorMoon:
The news is on.
It’s becoming my daily routine to check the news in the morning.

pages.ja:
「とくに目立った事件はないわね。 昨夜は出てこなかったんでしょう」
出てこなかった、とはあの“黒い影”のことだ。
「
ああ。連日無休ってワケじゃなさそうだな」
安堵しているのを隠して、そっけなく返答する。
pages.jaRuby:
「とくに目立った事件はないわね。 昨夜は出てこなかったんでしょう」

pages.en:
“There are no major incidents to report. So it didn't appear last night?”

By “it,” she means the “black shadow.”

“—Right. Apparently it doesn't operate every night without fail.”

I hide my relief behind a curt answer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“There aren’t any big stories. I guess it didn’t appear last night.”
She must mean the black shadow.
“Yeah. I guess it doesn’t come out every day.”
I answer, careful not to let my relief show.

pages.ja: 「そうね。百人単位の被害なんて、二日続けておきたらたまらないもの」
pages.jaRuby: 「そうね。百人単位の被害なんて、二日続けておきたらたまらないもの」
pages.en: “Apparently not. Casualties by the hundred two nights running would be more than anyone could bear.”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Yeah. I wouldn’t be able to bear hundreds of people getting hurt two days in a row.”

pages.ja:
朝の七時過ぎ。
居間には俺と遠坂しかいない。
桜は客間で眠っており、イリヤもまだ眠っている。
桜はともかくイリヤには起きてほしかったのだが、遠坂曰く疲れてるから休ませてやれ、なのだそうだ。
pages.jaRuby:

桜はともかくイリヤには起きてほしかったのだが、遠坂曰く疲れてるから休ませてやれ、なのだそうだ。
pages.en:
It is after seven in the morning.

Only Tohsaka and I are in the living room.

Sakura is sleeping in the guest room, and Illya has yet to wake.

Sakura aside, I had hoped Illya would join us. Tohsaka insisted she was exhausted and should be allowed to rest.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s past seven.
Tohsaka and I are the only ones in the living room.
Sakura and Illya are both sleeping.
I wanted Illya to wake up and come, but Tohsaka told me that she’s tired and I should let her rest.

pages.ja:
「
から、士郎も今夜に備えて休んでおいて」
唐突に遠坂が言う。
「……それは、どうして？」
pages.jaRuby:
「
から、士郎も今夜に備えて休んでおいて」
唐突に遠坂が言う。
「……それは、どうして？」
pages.en:
“—So you should rest too, Shirou. You need to be ready for tonight.”

Tohsaka says it without warning.

“…Why tonight?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“So you should rest too, in preparation for tonight.”
Tohsaka says this out of the blue.
“…Why?”

pages.ja:
「だから、例の切り札の作成。なんとか今日中に骨組みが出来るから、今夜“投影”を実行するわ。
で、成功次第臓硯と決着をつける。これ以上犠牲者は増やせない。あの影がなんであれ、臓硯を倒せば聖杯戦争は終わる。得体の知れないあの影も、そうなったら消えるでしょ」
pages.jaRuby:
「だから、例の切り札の作成。なんとか今日中に骨組みが出来るから、今夜“投影”を実行するわ。

pages.en:
“I mean the trump card we discussed. We'll somehow finish its framework today, and tonight you'll use Projection.

“Once it succeeds, we settle matters with Zouken. We cannot allow any more victims. Whatever that shadow is, defeating Zouken will end the Holy Grail War. Once that happens, the shadow should disappear too.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It’s the creation of our secret weapon. We’ll complete the framework today, so we’ll do the projection tonight.
We’ll go settle our match with Zouken as soon as we succeed. We can’t allow any more victims. No matter what that shadow may be, the Holy Grail War will end once we defeat Zouken. The mysterious shadow should disappear then.”

pages.ja:
「
遠坂。聖杯戦争が終われば、あの影は消えると思うのか」
pages.jaRuby:
「
遠坂。聖杯戦争が終われば、あの影は消えると思うのか」
pages.en: “—Tohsaka. Do you really think the shadow will disappear when the Holy Grail War ends?”
pages.mirrorMoon: “Tohsaka. You really think the shadow will disappear once the war is over?”

pages.ja:
「消えるわ。あいつの正体がなんであれ、アレが聖杯目的で現れているのは間違いない。
聖杯を欲しがっているのか、それとも聖杯に呼ばれているのかは判らない。けど、どっちにしたって原因は聖杯なんだから、聖杯さえなくなれば影は消えるのよ。
聖杯戦争が期限切れになるか、マスターが最後の一人になるか、それとも
聖杯の器になるモノが死んでしまえば、あの影は消え去るわ」

pages.en:
“It will. Whatever its true nature, there's no doubt it appeared because of the Holy Grail.

“I don't know whether it wants the Grail or the Grail is calling it. Either way, the Holy Grail is the cause. Once the Grail is gone, the shadow will disappear.

“Whether the Holy Grail War reaches its time limit, only one Master remains, or—the thing serving as the Grail's vessel dies, the shadow will vanish.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“It will. Whatever it is, I’m sure it appeared because of the Holy Grail.
I don’t know if it wants the Holy Grail, or if the Holy Grail summoned it. But either way, it’s here because of the Holy Grail, so it’ll disappear once the Holy Grail is gone.
In short, the shadow will disappear once the war ends.
That will happen when the time limit expires, when only one Master remains, orwhen the Holy Grail’s vessel dies.”

遠坂、おまえ」
……もう。
とっくの昔に、あの影の正体を知っていたのか。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“——Tohsaka. You…”

…Did she already know?

Has she known the shadow's identity all along?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Tohsaka, you”
…Already…
Knew what that shadow is?

「今のはただの推測よ。
臓硯を倒してもあの影は消えないかもしれない。
聖杯戦争が終わってもあの影は消えないかもしれない。
だから今は一番確実な方法をとる。手に入るかどうかも分からない聖杯なんかには頼れない。わたしたちはわたしたちだけの力で、臓硯とあの影を倒さないといけない」

pages.en:
“What I just said was only conjecture.

“The shadow may remain even if we defeat Zouken.

“It may remain even after the Holy Grail War ends.

“That's why we're taking the surest course available. We can't depend on a Holy Grail we may never obtain. We have to defeat Zouken and the shadow with our own strength.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I’m just guessing.
It might not disappear even if we defeat Zouken.
It might not disappear even when the war ends.
So I’m going to take the surest method. We can’t rely on uncertainties like obtaining the Holy Grail ourselves. We have to take down both Zouken and the shadow with our own powers.”

pages.ja:
言って、遠坂は席を立った。
何のつもりか、桜の為に用意した水差しと寝巻きを俺から取り上げて、だ。
pages.jaRuby:
言って、遠坂は席を立った。
何のつもりか、桜の為に用意した水差しと寝巻きを俺から取り上げて、だ。
pages.en:
With that, Tohsaka rises.

For some reason, she takes from me the pitcher of water and the nightclothes I had prepared for Sakura.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka gets up.
I don’t know why, but she takes the water jug and pajamas I prepared for Sakura.

pages.ja:
「おい。なんのつもりだよ、それ」
「桜の様子はわたしが見るわ。部屋も隣だし、あの子の看病はわたしの方が適任でしょう」
「む
いや、桜の看病は、俺が」
pages.jaRuby:

いや、桜の看病は、俺が」
pages.en:
“Hey. What do you think you're doing with those?”

“I'll check on Sakura. Our rooms are next to each other, and I'm better suited to nurse her.”

“Mm—but looking after Sakura is my—”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Hey, what are you doing?”
“I’ll go see how Sakura’s doing. Her room is next to mine, so I’m in a better position to look after her.”
“Heyno, I’ll take care of Sakura.”

pages.ja:
「馬鹿言わないで。士郎、一睡もしてないでしょ。そんな体でいられちゃわたしたちが困るってわからない？」
……？
一睡もしていないって、俺が？
pages.jaRuby:
「馬鹿言わないで。士郎、一睡もしてないでしょ。そんな体でいられちゃわたしたちが困るってわからない？」
……？
一睡もしていないって、俺が？
pages.en:
“Don't be ridiculous. Shirou, you haven't slept at all. Don't you understand how much trouble you cause us by walking around in that condition?”

…?

I haven't slept at all?
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t be stupid. You didn’t get any sleep last night, did you? Can’t you tell that you’ll be a liability in your condition?”
…?
I didn’t get any sleep?

pages.ja:
「それこそバカ言うなよ。昨日はちゃんと眠ったぞ、俺」
「呆れた。自覚がないほど参ってたワケ。
……まったく、嘘だと思うなら鏡を見てきなさい。顔面蒼白で目にクマ作ってたら、看病される桜だって気を遣うわ」
「な
それ、本当か？」

それ、本当か？」
pages.en:
“You're the one being ridiculous. I slept properly last night.”

“Unbelievable. You're so worn down you don't even realize it.

“…If you think I'm lying, look in a mirror. If you visit Sakura pale as death with shadows beneath your eyes, even she'll feel obliged to worry about you.”

“Wh—is that true?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t be stupid. I slept last night.”
“I don’t believe this. You’re so tired that you don’t even notice it?
…Geez, go look at the mirror if you think I’m lying. If you went to nurse Sakura with dark circles around your eyes and looking pale, it’d just make her worried.”
“Whatare you serious?”

pages.ja:
「うそ言ってどうするってのよ。もう、いいから士郎は部屋で休みなさい。夕方になったら呼びにいくから。
あ、眠れないなら手をかしてあげてもいいわよ？ ライダーの真似事でいいなら、まる一日前後不覚にしてあげられるけど？」
pages.jaRuby:
「うそ言ってどうするってのよ。もう、いいから士郎は部屋で休みなさい。夕方になったら呼びにいくから。

pages.en:
“Why would I lie? Enough. Go rest in your room, Shirou. I'll come for you this evening.

“Oh, if you can't sleep, I could lend a hand. If an imitation of Rider will do, I can knock you unconscious for about a full day.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Why would I lie? Geez, just go to your room and rest. I’ll go get you in the afternoon.
Oh, and if you can’t go to sleep, I can help you. If you don’t mind me copying Rider, I can put you under for about a day.”

つまり、遠坂は。

An imitation of Rider would mean an imitation of her Mystic Eyes. As far as I know, Tohsaka has no Mystic Eyes.

Which means—
pages.mirrorMoon:
Copying Rider means copying her mystic eyes. But as far as I know, Tohsaka doesn’t have mystic eyes.
In short, she’s…

pages.ja:
「それは、俺に実験台になれってコトか？」
「正解。今まで興味はなかったけど、魔眼も悪くないかなって。流石にあんな離れ業は無理だけど、眠りの暗示ぐらいなら即興で出来そうだなって」
pages.jaRuby:
「それは、俺に実験台になれってコトか？」

pages.en:
“Are you asking me to be your test subject?”

“Correct. They've never interested me before, but I'm beginning to see the appeal of Mystic Eyes. A feat like Rider's is beyond me, of course, but I think I could improvise a suggestion strong enough to put someone to sleep.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Are you telling me to be your guinea pig?”
“Exactly. I wasn’t interested before, but mystic eyes might not be that bad. I can’t do anything on that scale, but I might be able to do something like sleep suggestion.”

「
嘘つけ、何が魔眼も悪くないかな、だ。
おまえ、単にやられっぱなしじゃ気が済まないから練習したいだけだろ」
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“—Liar. What do you mean, you're beginning to see the appeal?

“You just can't stand having been on the receiving end and leaving it at that. You want to practice.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Don’t lie. What was that about them not being bad?
You just don’t want to stay defeated, so you want to learn it too, right?”

“Will you try it or not?”

“Of course not, idiot! I'm not taking part in an experiment that dangerous. Besides, if I sleep for an entire day, I won't wake until tomorrow morning.”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“J-Just be quiet! So, what about it?
Do you want to try it or not?”
“No, you idiot! I’m having nothing to do with such a dangerous experiment. First of all, if I sleep for a day, I can’t wake up until tomorrow morning.”

pages.ja:
「あ、そうか。うまくかかりすぎたら睡眠じゃなくて麻痺になるものね。士郎、単純だからかかりやすそうだし」
なるほど、と納得する遠坂。
なにげに反論したいが、それじゃ試してみる？ なんて言われそうなので黙っておく。
pages.jaRuby:

なるほど、と納得する遠坂。
なにげに反論したいが、それじゃ試してみる？ なんて言われそうなので黙っておく。
pages.en:
“Oh, right. If it worked too well, you might be paralyzed instead of asleep. And you're so simple-minded that you'd probably be especially susceptible.”

Tohsaka nods, satisfied with her reasoning.

I would like to object, but she would probably answer, “Then shall we test it?” So I hold my tongue.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh, right. It’ll be paralysis instead of sleep if it works too well. I think it’ll work well on you since you’re simple-minded.”
Tohsaka seems to be convinced.
I want to object, but I stay quiet since she might test it on me if I do object.

「まあ、それほど神経質ってワケでもないし、その気になれば簡単に眠れる。心配されるほどじゃない」
「そう？ なら桜の看病はわたしに任せて、士郎は部屋で大人しくできる？」
……と。
さっきまでの軽口から一転して、遠坂は真剣な目で訊ねてきた。

「まあ、それほど神経質ってワケでもないし、その気になれば簡単に眠れる。心配されるほどじゃない」

……と。
さっきまでの軽口から一転して、遠坂は真剣な目で訊ねてきた。
pages.en:
“I'm not that anxious. If I set my mind to it, I can fall asleep easily. You don't need to worry.”

“Can you? Then will you leave Sakura to me and behave yourself in your room?”

…Her bantering tone vanishes. Tohsaka fixes me with a serious gaze.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Well, I’m not that sensitive, so I can sleep if I want. You don’t have to worry about me.”
“Really? Then can you rest in your room and let me handle Sakura’s care?”
…Then.
Tohsaka drops her joking manner and asks me with serious eyes.

pages.en:
“…You're right. I'll shut myself away in my room for a while.

“I'll bring Sakura lunch and dinner. May I impose on you for everything else?”

“Of course. Leave Sakura to me. If she so much as tries to move without permission, I'll scold her back to sleep.

“But can you really fall asleep alone? Wouldn't you like me to try one little experiment after all?”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…You’re right. Then I’ll be in my room.
I’ll bring her lunch and dinner, so can you take care of her the rest of the time?”
“Yeah, you can leave her to me. I’ll scold her and put her back in bed if she tries to get up.
So, can you really sleep by yourself? Don’t you want to try it out once?”

pages.ja:
「しつこいな、そうゆう危なっかしいのは却下だ。
けどまあ、ありがとうな遠坂。気を遣わせて申し訳ない」
「べ、別に気なんか遣ってないけど。そ、それじゃわたしは行くから、士郎もちゃんと眠りなさいよねっ！」

pages.en:
“You're persistent. Dangerous experiments are out of the question.

“Still, thank you, Tohsaka. I'm sorry to make you worry.”

“I-I'm not worried at all! A-Anyway, I'm going now. Make sure you actually sleep, Shirou!”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“You’re persistent. I don’t want anything dangerous.
But thanks, Tohsaka. I’m sorry for making you look out for me.”
“I-I’m not looking out for you. I-I’m going, so you go sleep, okay!?”

pages.ja:
……まったく、なんというか。
勘が良いんだか悪いんだか、冷たいヤツなのか優しいヤツなのか。
天才肌の人間は相手を置いてけぼりにするっていうけど、あいつもその類だろう。
桜もタイヘンだ。遠坂が姉貴だなんて、俺だったら心休まる時がない。

pages.en:
…Honestly, I don't know what to make of her.

Is she perceptive or oblivious? Cold or kind?

They say a natural genius leaves everyone else behind. She must be that sort of person.

Sakura has my sympathy. If Tohsaka were my older sister, I doubt I'd ever know a moment's peace.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka leaves in a hurry.
…Man.
I don’t know if she’s perceptive or not, nor if she’s a good person or a cold person.
I hear geniuses tend to leave everyone else behind them, and I’m guessing that’s Tohsaka’s type.
Sakura has it tough. I’d never have peace of mind if Tohsaka were my older sister.

…Yes.

That's why I want the two of them to become sisters again as soon as possible.

“Well, I bet every day would be fun, though.”
…Right.
That’s why I want them back to being sisters as quickly as possible.

pages.ja:
この戦いが終わって、遠坂と間桐の約束事がなくなってしまえば、桜と遠坂は姉妹に戻れる。
十一年もの年月はそう簡単には埋まらないだろうが、それでも、少しずつ距離を縮めていって、何気ないことでも笑い合える仲になってほしい。

pages.en:
Once this war ends and the obligations between Tohsaka and Matou disappear, Sakura and Tohsaka can return to being sisters.

Eleven years cannot be bridged easily. Even so, I hope they'll close the distance little by little, until they can laugh together over the most ordinary things.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Sakura and Tohsaka can be together again once the war ends, and the promise between their families goes away.
The eleven-year gap won’t be bridged that easily, but I want them to get close enough to laugh together over trivial matters.

pages.jaRuby:

I'll do anything I can to help them.

I've thought it before, but I'm certain that would be the greatest gift Sakura could receive.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I’ll do anything to help.
I think this is the most I can do for Sakura.

Wait.

Without meaning to, I pictured Tohsaka smiling happily.

Sorry, Sakura… Does something like that count as cheating too?

Oh, crap.
I just imagined Tohsaka smiling happily.
I’m sorry, Sakura. Wait, does this count as being unfaithful?

戦いが終われば聖杯が現れる。
いや、厳密に言えば聖杯が“開かれる”。

…That could be bad.

Defeating Zouken would end the war.

Once the war ends, the Holy Grail will appear.

No—strictly speaking, the Grail will “open.”

Tohsaka said she’ll challenge Zouken tonight.
…That’s bad.
The war will end if we defeat Zouken.
The Holy Grail will appear once the war ends.
No, rather, the Holy Grail will be opened.

pages.ja:
聖杯は門だと臓硯は言った。
あらゆる望みを叶えるモノ、願望機は聖杯ではなく聖杯の中にあるものだと。
……それが確かなら、聖杯である桜はどうなるのか。
イリヤは言った。
聖杯として完成に近づけば近づくほど、桜は人間としての機能を失うのだと。

pages.en:
Zouken said the Holy Grail was a gate.

The thing capable of granting every wish—the wish-granting device—was not the Grail itself, but what lay inside it.

…If that is true, what will happen to Sakura, who is the Holy Grail?

Illya told me that the closer Sakura comes to completion as the Grail, the more of her human functions she will lose.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Zouken said the Holy Grail is a gate.
What grants the wishes is not the Holy Grail, but what’s inside of it.
…If that’s true, what will happen to Sakura, who is the Holy Grail?
Illya said that…
Sakura loses her human functions as she nears completion as a Holy Grail.

pages.ja:
……これが後者なら問題はない。
臓硯を倒し、桜を脅かす存在を排除して、戦いの期限切れを待てばいいのだ。
pages.jaRuby:

We can defeat Zouken, eliminate the threat to Sakura, and wait for the war to expire.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…There’s no problem if it’s the latter.
I just have to defeat Zouken, eliminate what’s threatening Sakura, and wait for the duration of the war.

pages.ja:
遠坂は今夜のうちに臓硯に挑むと言った。
なら臓硯は倒せる。
あいつが戦うと言うからには、高い勝算があるという事だ。
pages.jaRuby:
遠坂は今夜のうちに臓硯に挑むと言った。
なら臓硯は倒せる。
あいつが戦うと言うからには、高い勝算があるという事だ。
pages.en:
Tohsaka said she would challenge Zouken tonight.

Then Zouken can be defeated.

If she says she will fight, it means she believes the odds are firmly in her favor.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka said we’ll challenge Zouken tonight.
Then we can beat Zouken.
If she says we’re fighting, that means we have a high chance of winning.

pages.ja:
「……となると、問題は一つだけ」
……あの“黒い影”。
臓硯を倒したところであいつは消えない。
あいつは桜という聖杯があるかぎり現れ続ける。
そうして現れる度、多くの命を奪っていく。
戦いの期限切れを待つ、という事はあの影を放置する、という事。
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
“…Then there is only one problem.”

…The “black shadow.”

It will not disappear merely because Zouken dies.

As long as the Holy Grail called Sakura exists, it will continue to appear.

And each time it does, it will take countless lives.

Waiting for the war to expire means leaving the shadow unchecked.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Then there’s only one problem.”
…The black shadow.
Beating Zouken won’t make it disappear.
It will continue to surface as long as the Holy Grail, Sakura, exists.
And it will take many lives every time.
Waiting for the deadline means doing nothing about that shadow.

pages.ja:
「……倒す、しかない。あの影を、俺の手で倒す」
……それ以外に方法はない。
だが倒せるのか。
アレが聖杯の中からこぼれてくるモノだとしたら、影自体には死の概念はないだろう。
もしアレを消せるとしたら、それは投影機である桜本人を消すか、投影機に魔力を送っている本体を消すしかないのではないか。
pages.jaRuby:
「……倒す、しかない。あの影を、俺の手で倒す」

pages.en:
“…I have no choice but to defeat it. I'll destroy that shadow with my own hands.”

…There is no other way.

But can it be defeated?

If it is something spilling from inside the Holy Grail, the shadow itself may have no concept of death.

Perhaps the only way to erase it is to destroy Sakura, the projector that gives it form—or destroy the true body feeding magical energy into that projector, like electrical current into a machine.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I have to defeat it. I have to defeat the shadow myself.”
…That’s the only possible choice.
But can I beat it?
If that thing came from the Holy Grail, the shadow should not have a concept of death.
If I’m to eliminate it, I have to eliminate the projector, Sakura herself, or destroy the main body that’s sending magical energy to the projector.

pages.ja:
「……本体、か……」
……そんなものがいるとは思えない。
だがそう考える以外、確かな打開策がない。
pages.jaRuby:
「……本体、か……」
……そんなものがいるとは思えない。
だがそう考える以外、確かな打開策がない。
pages.en:
“…Its true body…”

…I cannot imagine that such a thing exists.

Yet without that possibility, I have no concrete path forward.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…Main body, huh…?”
…I don’t think such a thing exists.
But I can’t come up with any effective plans unless I assume so.

pages.ja:
「
言峰。あいつは、その事に気がつかなかったのか……！？」
そんな筈あるか……！
あいつは桜から刻印虫を摘出した。
少量だが刻印虫を取り出し、桜の体を治療したのだ。

pages.en:
“—Kotomine. Did he really fail to notice…!?”

Impossible…!

He extracted the Crest Worms from Sakura.

He removed a small number of them and treated her body.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Kotomine. He didn’t notice that…!?”
No way…!
He extracted some crest worm from Sakura.
He removed just a small quantity, but he treated Sakura’s body.

pages.ja:
そこまでしておいて気がつかない筈がない。
仮にも聖杯戦争の監督役であり、前回の戦いで最後まで残ったマスターだ。
なら、桜の体の異状に気がついて然るべきだろう……！
pages.jaRuby:

pages.en:
After going that far, there is no possibility he failed to notice.

For all his faults, he is the overseer of the Holy Grail War and a Master who survived until the end of the previous conflict.

He should have recognized the abnormality within Sakura's body…!
pages.mirrorMoon:
There’s no way he wouldn’t notice.
He’s the supervisor of the Holy Grail War, and he was one of the last surviving Masters in the previous war.
Then he should know what’s wrong with her body…!

「っ、は
！」
玄関を飛び出る。
突然の閃きに全身を支配されて、あの神父の顔しか思い浮かばなくなっている。

pages.en:
“Hah—!”

I burst through the front door.

The sudden realization consumes me completely. I can think of nothing but the priest's face.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Haa!”
I run out the door.
Compelled by the sudden insight, I can only think about the priest.

pages.ja:
「くそ、どうしてもっと早く気付かなかった……！」
考えればすぐに思い至った筈だ。
桜の無意識の姿で現れる影、
“聖杯”の中にあるモノがなんであるかを、あの男なら知っている筈なんだから
！

pages.en:
“Damn it! Why didn't I realize sooner…!?”

A moment's thought should have led me there.

The shadow that takes shape through Sakura's unconscious mind—

that man must know what lies within the “Holy Grail”—!
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Damn, why didn’t I realize earlier…!?”
If I’d just thought about it, I would’ve seen it right away.
The shadow that appears as Sakura’s subconscious form.
That man should know what’s inside the Holy Grail!
